init.title: Shelly Cloud DIY options
init.description: Adjust how often the integration polls Shelly Cloud for state, when a silent device counts as offline and, optionally, the local gateway URL used by the historical-data service. Device selection follows on the next step.

data.offline_after_minutes: Report a device as offline after (minutes)
data.local_gateway_url: Local gateway URL (optional, for EM historical data)

data_description.poll_interval: 3–60 s. Lower values feel snappier but consume more of Shelly's 1 req/s rate-limit budget.
data_description.offline_after_minutes: 2–1440 min, default 30. Each device's "Reporting" sensor turns off once the device has been silent this long. It is only a base value: a device that is naturally quieter earns a wider window on its own, and battery or BLE devices are handled separately. Lowering it therefore mainly speeds up detection on devices that report continuously, such as power-metering plugs.
data_description.local_gateway_url: Only needed if you use a local Shelly gateway to back-fill historical energy data.

download_and_convert_history.name: Download and convert historical energy data
download_and_convert_history.description: Fetches CSV exports from the local Shelly gateway and imports them into Home Assistant's long-term statistics.

gateway_url.name: Gateway URL
gateway_url.description: Base URL of the local gateway (overrides the one configured in options).

device_id.name: Device ID
device_id.description: Optional — restrict the import to a single EM device. All EM devices are imported if omitted.

replace_device.name: Replace device
replace_device.description: Transplant a dead Shelly's Home Assistant identity (entity IDs, the HA device, name, area, history and every automation/dashboard reference) onto a new Shelly of the same model, so you don't have to reconfigure Home Assistant after a hardware swap. Enable the new device first.

old_device.name: Old (replaced) device
old_device.description: The Shelly device that broke or was removed.

new_device.name: New device
new_device.description: The new Shelly that should take over. Enable it first.

dry_run.name: Dry run
dry_run.description: Only show what would change, without applying it.

force.name: Force (ignore model mismatch)
force.description: Proceed even if the two devices report different models. Only use this if the channel layout matches.

fleet_map.name: Fleet map
fleet_map.description: Read-only overlay: matches every cloud device to its local (native Shelly) twin by MAC, suggests names, and flags any device whose control runs over the cloud. Writes a report to your notifications. Safe to run anytime — it changes nothing unless you explicitly opt in.

dry_run.name: Dry run
dry_run.description: Only show the report, without applying any native name suggestions. On by default.

apply_native_name_suggestions.name: Apply native name suggestions
apply_native_name_suggestions.description: Also copy each cloud alias onto its matched local (native Shelly) device. Only writes the technical name, never a name you set yourself. Requires turning Dry run off. Off by default.

options.manual: Manual selection — Submit saves the list below
options.all: Tick all devices (Submit updates the list — does not save yet)
options.none: Untick all devices (Submit updates the list — does not save yet)

rate_limited.title: Shelly Cloud is rate-limiting this integration
rate_limited.description:
Shelly Cloud allows about one request per second, and it has been rejecting this integration's requests ({entry_title}) for the last couple of minutes.

**This is not a problem with your Authorization cloud key.** Shelly signals the rate limit as an HTTP 401 response whose body contains `max_req` — the same status code a rejected key would produce, but a different cause. Nothing needs to be re-entered.

What to do:

1. Check whether something else is polling Shelly Cloud with the same key at the same time — the Shelly mobile app, a second Home Assistant entry for the same account, or your own scripts.
2. Raise the poll interval in the integration options (Settings → Devices & services → Shelly Cloud DIY → Configure). The default of 5 seconds leaves room, but the integration also makes occasional extra lookups on top of each poll.

Entities become available again on the first poll that gets through, and this message disappears on its own.

missing_devices.title: Selected devices are missing from your Shelly account
missing_devices.description:
You selected {count} device(s) for {entry_title} that Shelly Cloud has not reported for the last 24 hours, so no entities are created for them.

Device(s): {device_ids}

The most likely causes are that the device was removed from your Shelly account, or — for a Shelly BLU device — that the Bluetooth gateway bridging it has been offline for a long time.

What to do:

1. If this is a Shelly BLU device, check that the mains-powered Shelly that bridges it is online.
2. Otherwise, check whether the device still appears in the Shelly app under the same account.
3. If it is gone for good, open Settings → Devices & services → Shelly Cloud DIY → Configure, click through to the device list and save. The missing device is no longer offered there, so it drops out of your selection automatically. Then run the **Find Shelly devices no longer in your account** action (Developer tools → Actions, leave Dry run on) to see which Home Assistant devices are left over.

This message clears by itself as soon as the device reports again, or after you save your device selection again.

history_import_failed.title: Historical energy data could not be imported
history_import_failed.description:
The historical-data sync for {entry_title} has run twice without importing anything. Live device data is unaffected — only the import of past energy readings into long-term statistics.

Most often the local gateway URL is wrong, or the gateway is not reachable from Home Assistant.

What to do:

1. Open Settings → Devices & services → Shelly Cloud DIY → Configure and check the local gateway URL, including the scheme and port (for example `http://192.168.1.50:8080`).
2. Confirm the gateway is running and reachable from Home Assistant.
3. If you no longer use it, clear the field to switch the import off.

The sync runs once at startup and then daily. To check a correction right away, run the **Download and convert historical energy data** action from Developer tools → Actions instead of waiting.
